note: First verdict 2026-11-20 by an independent agent. RFC 4301 Section 7.4: "All implementations MUST support stateful fragment checking to accommodate BYPASS traffic for which a non-trivial port range is specified." What the tags prove: TestPortScopedBypassNeverReachesTheForwardPath and TestPortScopedBypassForwardPathFollowsFragmentGathering (spdEntryHasTransit revert records) that a port-scoped BYPASS reaches FWD only when the dataplane reports fragment gathering; TestXFRMPortScopedBypassIsNeverStoredOnTheForwardPath that the kernel stores the in and out halves in IN and OUT; TestRFC4301ForwardedFragmentsRespectOperatorDisposition, on Ze's kernel with a revert record on spdForwardGathers, that under unmatched discard a whole and a fragmented IPv4 datagram on the one-port bypass cross while a lone non-initial fragment on that port and a fragmented datagram to an unnamed port do not. The negative TestAnyPortBypassReachesTheForwardPath is the case just outside the clause (both ports any reach FWD on a non-gathering dataplane, a local port does not). Why weak and not enforced: the row claims the whole requirement with no annotation, and two cases it covers cannot turn any tagged test red. spdEntryHasTransit projects a port-scoped bypass onto FWD for IPv6 as well under capability bit 3, and the IPv6 gather (xfrm6_fragment_prerouting, gokrazy/kernel/patches/0005-xfrm-fragment-guard.patch) is observed by no tagged packet test, since the forward lab disables IPv6. The IN direction rests on Linux running ip_defrag before the LOCAL_IN policy check, read from the kernel source in the summary and asserted by no packet test on a port-scoped IN bypass. A {partial} split by case (IPv4 forward tested; IPv6 forward and local delivery the gap) would make the scope honest.
